topic_ko: 글의 독자는 친밀함이 아니라 비판적 통찰로 고르라
_note: 주장(논설문) FULL set. 유형마다 passage 를 다르게 paraphrase. grammar/vocab/blank/implication 의 밑줄·빈칸·함축 어구는 해당 passage 문장에 글자 그대로 존재.

passage: A story should leave your desk for another reader's hands only after you are satisfied that you have given it everything you have.
It is natural to hand it first to the people you love most, and there is no harm in that.
Yet in most cases their reading will not push the work forward in any meaningful way.
The comments that truly improve a manuscript tend to come from elsewhere.
Readers should be selected for the sharpness of their judgment, not for how dear they are to you.
Other writers are the natural choice, though not every writer is equally useful.
In a writing class or circle you soon learn whose pages you respect.
You also learn, from experience, whose comments once helped you and whose merely flattered you.
choices: practical ways to finish a first draft faster than usual
the danger of revising a manuscript too many times
how writing classes teach students to become better editors
why writers should pick readers for judgment rather than closeness
the reason family members enjoy reading unpublished stories
theme.explanation_ko: 글은 '가까운 사람의 감상이 아니라 비판적 판단력을 갖춘 독자에게서 피드백을 받아야 한다'는 내용이다. 판단력을 기준으로 독자를 골라야 하는 이유를 말한 ④가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①초고 완성 속도, ②과도한 퇴고의 위험, ③글쓰기 수업의 편집 교육, ⑤가족이 원고를 즐기는 이유는 모두 본문 초점이 아니다.

passage: Do not show your story to anyone until you are content that you have done everything you could for it.
Showing it to family and close friends is perfectly fine as a pleasure, but it is a poor way to improve the work.
Affection makes honest criticism difficult, and praise from loved ones rarely reveals what is broken.
The most useful responses usually come from readers with no stake in your feelings.
Therefore, pick your readers for the sharpness of their critical eye rather than for their nearness to you.
Other writers make good candidates, but do not assume that any writer will serve.
Within a class or a writing group you will discover whose work you genuinely admire.
Past experience will also tell you whose comments truly helped and whose did not.
choices: 완성된 원고는 가능한 한 많은 사람에게 두루 보여 주어야 한다.
글에 대한 피드백은 비판적 안목을 지닌 사람에게 구해야 한다.
가족의 칭찬을 통해 글쓰기의 자신감을 먼저 길러야 한다.
작가는 자신의 판단만 믿고 타인의 조언을 멀리해야 한다.
글쓰기 모임에는 되도록 많은 동료 작가를 참여시켜야 한다.
claim.explanation_ko: 다섯 번째 문장 'pick your readers for the sharpness of their critical eye rather than for their nearness to you'가 필자의 주장이다. 비판적 안목을 지닌 사람에게 피드백을 구하라는 ②가 정답.
claim.distractor_ko: ①두루 보여 주기, ③가족의 칭찬으로 자신감 기르기, ④타인의 조언 배척, ⑤모임 인원 확대는 모두 본문 주장과 다르다.

passage: Hand your story over only when you are sure it has already received your best effort.
Your closest people will gladly read it, and that pleasure is worth something.
But their comments seldom carry the work any further than it already stands.
Valuable feedback comes from readers who can see the writing rather than the writer.
So the criterion for choosing a reader should be critical insight, never intimacy.
Other writers are ideal readers, yet not all of them are equally discerning.
Time spent in a writing group tells you whose work deserves your respect.
It also tells you whose past advice actually made your writing better.
choices: 글은 미완성 단계에서 자주 공유할수록 빨리 좋아진다.
가까운 사람의 칭찬이야말로 글쓰기의 가장 큰 원동력이다.
동료 작가라면 누구에게 보여 주어도 결과는 비슷하다.
글쓰기 모임은 인맥을 넓히는 수단으로 활용해야 한다.
피드백은 친밀함이 아니라 비판적 통찰을 기준으로 구해야 한다.
gist.explanation_ko: 가까운 사람의 감상은 작품을 앞으로 나아가게 하지 못하므로, 비판적 통찰을 기준으로 독자를 골라야 한다는 것이 요지이다. ⑤가 정답.
gist.distractor_ko: ①미완성 단계 공유는 첫 문장이 반대하고, ②③④는 본문이 부정하거나 언급하지 않은 내용이다.

passage: A manuscript is ready for other eyes only when its author is satisfied that nothing more can be done alone.
Loved ones will read it warmly, and there is nothing wrong with that.
Their warmth, however, is exactly what makes their reading unreliable as a tool for revision.
The feedback that changes a story usually comes from readers chosen for a different reason.
That reason is critical insight, not closeness.
Other writers often qualify, but the label writer alone guarantees nothing.
A writing circle quickly shows you whose pages you admire and whose you do not.
Experience of past feedback shows you whose opinions were worth having.
choices: Write First, Revise Later: A Simple Rule
How to Build a Supportive Circle of Friends
Pick Readers for Insight, Not for Affection
Why Every Writer Needs a Professional Editor
The Joy of Sharing Stories with Your Family
title.explanation_ko: 독자를 고르는 기준이 애정이 아니라 비판적 통찰이어야 한다는 글의 핵심을 압축한 ③이 제목으로 적절하다.
title.distractor_ko: ①퇴고 시점 규칙, ②우호적 모임 만들기, ④전문 편집자 고용, ⑤가족과의 공유의 즐거움은 모두 글의 중심이 아니다.

passage: Show your story to others only after you are happy that you have done your very best for it.
You will probably want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that is fine.
In most cases, though, you should not look to their reading for any great benefit to your work.
The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources entirely.
You should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you.
Fellow writers are ideal, but do not imagine that any writer will do.
In a writers' circle you will know whose writing you admire and whose opinions once helped.
In the end, a warm mirror shows you nothing you did not already believe.
implication.underlined: a warm mirror shows you nothing you did not already believe
choices: readers who are fond of you merely confirm your own view of the work
writers should avoid rereading their own drafts too often
honest criticism is only possible between complete strangers
a story improves whenever it is read by a larger audience
praise is more motivating than criticism for beginning writers
implication.explanation_ko: '따뜻한 거울'은 애정 때문에 있는 그대로를 비추지 못하고 작가가 이미 믿고 있던 것만 되돌려 주는 가까운 독자를 뜻한다. 즉 애정 어린 독자는 자기 생각을 확인해 줄 뿐이라는 ①이 정답.
implication.distractor_ko: ②초고 재독 습관, ③완전한 타인만이 비평 가능, ④독자 수 증가, ⑤칭찬의 동기 부여 효과는 이 비유가 뜻하는 바가 아니다.

passage: Only when you are happy that you have done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else.
You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that is fine.
In most cases, however, you should not look to their reading for any great benefit to your work.
The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources.
You should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you.
Fellow writers are ideal, but do not imagine that any writer will do.
If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you will know whose writing you admire.
If you have had feedback in the past, you will know who opinions have been helpful and whose have not.
grammar.explanation_ko: ⑤ 뒤에 명사 opinions 가 이어지므로 소유를 나타내는 의문사 whose 가 와야 한다. 주격 who 는 뒤에 명사를 직접 취할 수 없다 → whose opinions. 정답 ⑤.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①Only + 부사절이 문두에 와 주절이 도치된 should you show, ②조동사 should not 뒤의 동사원형 look, ③be likely to V 구문의 likely, ④부정 명령문 do not imagine 은 모두 옳다.

passage: Show your story to someone else only when you are happy that you have done the best you can for it.
You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that is fine.
In most cases, however, you should not look to their reading for any great benefit to your work.
The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources.
You should choose readers for their emotional attachment, not their critical insight.
Fellow writers are ideal, but do not imagine that any writer will do.
If you belong to a writers' circle, you will know whose writing you admire.
Past experience will also tell you whose opinions have been helpful.
vocab.explanation_ko: ③ 글은 친밀함이 아니라 비판적 통찰을 기준으로 독자를 고르라고 말한다. 따라서 '정서적 애착(emotional attachment)'을 기준으로 고르라는 것은 정반대이며, critical insight 로 고쳐야 한다. 정답 ③.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①benefit(도움), ②valuable(값진), ④ideal(이상적인), ⑤admire(존경하다)는 모두 문맥에 적절하다.

passage: A story is ready for other readers only when you are satisfied that you have given it your best.
You will naturally want to share it with those you love, and that does no harm.
But affection blunts judgment, and praise from close readers rarely tells you what is wrong.
The comments that genuinely improve a manuscript come from elsewhere.
Fellow writers often qualify, yet the title of writer alone guarantees nothing.
In a writing group you soon learn whose pages you admire and whose advice once helped.
Use that record, not your feelings, when deciding whom to trust with your draft.
In short, readers should be chosen for their __________________, not for their nearness to you.
blank.explanation_ko: 글 전체가 애정이 아닌 판단력을 기준으로 독자를 고르라고 말하므로, 빈칸에는 '비판적 통찰(critical insight)'이 들어간다.
blank.distractor_ko: ①읽는 속도, ②출간 이력, ③후한 칭찬, ⑤공통 관심사는 모두 본문이 제시한 선택 기준이 아니다.

irrelevant.intro: You should show your story to someone else only after you are satisfied that you have done your best for it.
sentences: You may well want to show it first to your nearest and dearest, and that is perfectly fine.
In most cases, however, their reading will bring no great benefit to the work itself.
Most bestselling novels are published in the autumn, when bookshop traffic reaches its yearly peak.
The most valuable feedback comes from readers chosen for their critical insight, not their closeness to you.
Fellow writers are ideal for this, though you should not assume that any writer will do.
irrelevant.explanation_ko: 글은 '누구에게 피드백을 받을 것인가'를 다루는데, ③ '베스트셀러는 가을에 출간된다'는 출간 시기와 서점 방문객에 관한 내용으로 주제와 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ①②④⑤는 모두 가까운 사람의 한계와 비판적 통찰을 지닌 독자 선택이라는 흐름으로 자연스럽게 이어진다.

order.given: Only when you are happy that you have done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else.

blocks.A: The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you.
blocks.B: Fellow writers are ideal, but do not imagine that any writer will do. In a writers' circle you will soon know whose opinions have been helpful and whose have not.
blocks.C: You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that is fine, but in most cases you should not look to their reading for any great benefit to your work.

order.explanation_ko: 언제 보여 줄지(주어진 글) 다음에 (C)에서 가까운 사람에게 보여 주는 것의 한계를 지적하고, (A)에서 그렇다면 어떤 기준으로 독자를 골라야 하는지 제시한 뒤, (B)에서 그 기준을 실제로 적용하는 방법을 설명한다. (C)-(A)-(B).
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 '다른 원천(other sources)'은 가까운 사람의 한계(C)가 먼저 나와야 성립하고, (B)의 동료 작가 이야기는 선택 기준(A)이 제시된 뒤에 와야 한다.

insert.insert_sentence: The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources.

passage_marked.text: Only when you are happy that you have done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else.
You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that is fine, but in most cases you should not look to their reading for any great benefit to your work.
You should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you.
Fellow writers are ideal, but do not imagine that any writer will do.
In a writers' circle you will know whose opinions have been helpful and whose have not.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 other sources 는 '가까운 사람의 읽기로는 큰 도움을 얻지 못한다'는 ②앞 문장을 받아 대안을 제시하고, 곧이어 그 기준(비판적 통찰)이 구체화된다. 따라서 ②가 정답.
insert.distractor_ko: ①에 넣으면 대비될 '가까운 사람'이 아직 언급되지 않아 other sources 가 무엇의 대안인지 알 수 없고, ③ 이후는 이미 선택 기준이 제시된 뒤라 늦다.

passage: Show your story to others only after you are satisfied that you have done your best for it.
It is natural to give it first to the people closest to you, and that is harmless enough.
Their reading, however, rarely brings any great benefit to the work.
The most valuable feedback tends to come from other sources.
Readers should be chosen for their critical insight, not their closeness to you.
Fellow writers are ideal, though not every writer will do.
A writing circle teaches you whose writing you admire.
Past feedback teaches you whose opinions have been helpful and whose have not.
summary.summary_template: Because affection tends to make a reader's response __(A)__, a writer should select readers according to their capacity for __(B)__ judgment rather than their personal nearness.
summary.explanation_ko: 친밀함은 반응을 (A)도움이 되지 않게(unhelpful) 만들므로, 작가는 개인적 친밀함이 아니라 (B)비판적(critical) 판단 능력을 기준으로 독자를 골라야 한다. ③이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A) 가까운 독자의 반응은 가혹(harsh)하거나 정직(honest)한 것이 아니라 도움이 되지 않는 것이고, (B) 기준은 감정적(emotional) 판단이 아니라 비판적(critical) 판단이다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 당신은 독자를 당신과의 친밀함이 아니라 그들의 비판적 통찰을 기준으로 골라야 한다.
writing.answer: You should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you.
writing.explanation_ko: choose A for B(B를 기준으로 A를 고르다) 구문에 not B'로 대조를 덧붙인 구조.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 동료 작가들이 이상적이지만, 아무 작가나 괜찮을 것이라고 생각하지는 말라.
writing.answer: Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do.
writing.explanation_ko: 부정 명령문 don't + 동사원형(imagine), 긍정문의 any(어떤 ~라도), will do(괜찮다·충분하다).

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 당신의 이야기를 위해 할 수 있는 최선을 다했다고 만족할 때에만 그것을 다른 사람에게 보여 주어야 한다.
conditions: the best you can 을 사용할 것
writing.answer: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else.
writing.explanation_ko: Only + 부사절이 문두에 오면 주절의 조동사가 주어 앞으로 나가 도치된다(should you show).

writing.question: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other ___________.
writing.explanation_ko: 가장 값진 피드백은 가까운 사람이 아닌 다른 '원천(sources)'에서 온다고 했으며, 본문 세 번째 문장에 그대로 등장한다.

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work.
writing.answer: 당신은 가장 가깝고 소중한 사람들에게 그것을 보여 주고 싶을 수도 있고 그것도 괜찮지만, 대부분의 경우 그들의 읽기에서 당신의 작품에 큰 도움이 될 만한 것을 기대해서는 안 된다.
writing.explanation_ko: may well(아마 ~일 것이다), nearest and dearest(가장 가깝고 소중한 사람들), look to A for B(A에게서 B를 기대하다).

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 이 글의 주제문을 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이 글에서 필자가 주장하는 바를 영어 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
conditions: critical insight 와 closeness 를 모두 사용할 것
writing.answer: Writers should choose their readers for critical insight rather than for closeness to themselves.
writing.explanation_ko: 선택 기준을 대조하는 A rather than B 구조로 필자의 주장(비판적 통찰 > 친밀함)을 압축한다.
